evidenceRetention: Failed/interrupted JSON records are retained, and current verification scripts write timestamped copies. One earlier successful GPU-fixture plain JSON was overwritten before timestamping was added. Four initial failed antipode PNGs were overwritten by the successful run; an actual offscreen-camera reproduction image is retained and explicitly labeled. Current Globe screenshots and JSON are also archived under runs/<timestamp>. Missing earlier originals are not reconstructed.

performance.basis: median of three warm run medians; each run uses the same three sun directions
performance.baselineLimitation: A uses original revision visibility GLSL and median BVH within the new lifecycle/runtime. Initialization retains full-domain probe tracing; not a byte-identical full baseline build.
performance.timingScope: GPU accumulated work vs CPU first/final submission reported independently. Neither is physical presentation latency.

result.note: A deferral ends submission for that frame after at least one batch because the next stage has no asynchronous GPU cost estimate. It is not a blocked GPU/CPU wait. Warm direction updates can have zero such deferrals. Diagnostic wrapping overhead excludes this run from speed claims.

coverage: GI covers resident local building/foundation/proxy triangles. Globe imagery and surrounding terrain do not participate in complete indirect transport.
limitations: Real ion imagery/terrain activation remains unverified without a token.
Probe interpolation can leave dark blotches near corners and small objects; screenshots are evidence, not a claim of visual parity with another renderer.

Ground shadows can visually separate from the foundation. Stable Globe triangle-mesh contact is checked separately; a normal-offset diagnostic did not establish a safe visible improvement, so shadow defaults are retained.
Isolated A/B and independently rebuilt original baseline are distinct experiments; see cleanBaseline status and raw results.
No dynamic geometry, Tiles GI, SDF, Cards, SSGI, reflections or WebGPU.
